subject: SIG: incident response notification windows and evidence routing clarification
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-corp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCloud Audit Team <vendor-audit@brightcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: incident notification windows and evidence requests

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the SIG questionnaire submission last week — quick follow-up from our security team about incident response (section 4). They asked for: 1) the contractual notification windows Redwood observes for customer-impacting incidents, and 2) an expected timeline for when we can receive primary evidence (playbook excerpt, timeline logs) if an incident were to affect Acme systems.

Could you confirm the standard notice windows (e.g., 72 hours, 7 days depending on severity) and who on your side is the point of contact for urgent evidence collection? Our compliance team needs this to close the review.

Appreciate a short timeline we can include in our audit notes.

Best,
Priya Sharma
Security Operations Lead
Acme Corp

--
Attachments: none

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-corp.com>
Cc: BrightCloud Audit Team <vendor-audit@brightcloud.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: incident notification windows and evidence requests

Priya — thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers below so you have something to include in the audit notes; copying our IR engineer Neha for evidence-routing details and next steps.

1) Notification windows:
- Critical (active data exfiltration, confirmed customer impact): initial notification within 24 hours of confirmation; follow-ups as evidence becomes available.
- High (service degradation affecting customer traffic but no confirmed data loss): initial notification within 72 hours.
- Medium/Low (internal impact, no customer effect): notification in the next reporting cycle (up to 7 days) unless otherwise requested.

These windows reflect our standard contractual commitments for Hosted API customers; Dedicated/Private customers may have tailored SLAs in their contracts. If Acme requires a faster contractual window, we can discuss during the contract review.

2) Evidence/timeline delivery:
- Playbook excerpt and process documentation: same business day for critical incidents, 1–2 business days otherwise (PDF extract; redacted where necessary).
- Forter logs / request traces: depends on log retention and scope; typical delivery window for a targeted log pull is 3–5 business days.
- Forensic images or raw artifacts: negotiated case-by-case under a data-sharing agreement; expect 2–4 weeks.

POC for urgent evidence requests: Neha Kapoor (Security Engineer, IR lead) — neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, +1 (415) 555-0192. For legal/contract matters, Laura Bennett (Sr. Counsel) is on copy.

I can put these bullets into a short formal statement for the SIG response if that helps.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

--

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-corp.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: incident notification windows and evidence requests

Priya — looping in legal briefly. A couple of quick clarifications to avoid confusion in the audit notes:

- "Initial notification" above refers to the time we confirm customer impact; our detection and validation window means we cannot give an absolute discovery time guarantee. Please reflect as "initial notification within X hours of confirmed customer-impacting incident."
- For Acme specifically, any change to notice windows would be a contractual amendment. If you are relying on the SIG answer as an enforced SLA, flag that now and we'll coordinate commercial/legal.

Rishi — can you confirm whether the "3–5 business days" for log pulls is standard for Hosted customers or if that depends on the log type/retention tier?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: incident notification windows and evidence requests

Priya — following up with a tidy summary you can paste into the SIG response. We also attached the SOC2 report and a short evidence checklist for your convenience.

Summary for SIG:
- Notification windows: Critical — initial notification within 24 hours of confirmed customer-impacting incident; High — initial notification within 72 hours of confirmation; Medium/Low — notification within 7 days. These are our standard Hosted commitments; contractual terms may differ for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Evidence routing & expected delivery: playbook excerpt (same business day for Critical; 1–2 business days otherwise); targeted log pulls (3–5 business days depending on retention and scope); forensic/raw artifacts (case-by-case; typically 2–4 weeks and require an NDA/evidence-sharing addendum).
- Primary POC for urgent evidence requests: Neha Kapoor (neha_kapoor@redwood.ai). For legal questions: Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwood.ai).

Attachments included (stubs):
- SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026.pdf (SOC 2 report; redacted public copy)
- IR-Playbook-excerpt.pdf (two-page excerpt describing detection/validation/notification flow)
- evidence-collection-checklist.csv (checklist — what logs we can provide and typical time-to-delivery)

If Acme would like language that elevates any of these into contractually binding SLAs, please mark the SIG response and we will route to commercial/legal immediately.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Logan Wright
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
